content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through validating common input types with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns email format checks into a repeatable implementation choice. Read values with .val(), validate to guide the user, and display actionable errors. Client-side validation never replaces server-side validation or authorization.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
